title: Object-relative ultraviolet weighting of electromagnetic modes and one-loop ultraviolet finiteness in quantum electrodynamics
abstract: This work explores whether localized electromagnetic interactions can be modeled in terms of an effective object-relative ultraviolet weighting of internal modes. The proposal is motivated heuristically by two considerations: a weak-field self-backreaction estimate for sufficiently localized energy-carrying modes and a three-dimensional overlap argument for localized interactions. In the resulting ansatz, the infrared sector remains unchanged up to a characteristic scale the at angular wavenumber $k_c$, while ultraviolet contributions are suppressed asymptotically by a factor of order $k_c^3/k^3$ with the angular wavenumber $k$. Because a crossover based solely on $k^μk_μ$ is not well suited to the intended mode-based interpretation, the weighting is formulated in terms of the object-relative covariant mode variable $u_μ k^μ$ with the four-velocity $u^μ$, i.e. the mode frequency measured in the rest frame of the localized interaction object. Within this restricted framework, selected one-loop QED contributions considered here become ultraviolet finite, and a restricted one-loop Ward-consistency check is preserved when the same scalar weighting is assigned consistently to the same internal photon mode in self-energy and vertex corrections. Four initial test cases are discussed: the anomalous magnetic moment, a Bethe-type low-energy Lamb-shift estimate, the Casimir effect, and a compact ultraviolet one-loop test. In the first three cases, the weighting leads to physically sensible characteristic scales associated with the electron Compton scale, an atomic bound-state scale, and plate distance, respectively. The results suggest that different observables may probe different effective localization scales. Action-level derivation, spectral consistency, and extension beyond one loop remain open problems.
summary: This theoretical paper proposes a novel method to regularize ultraviolet divergences in Quantum Electrodynamics by applying an object-relative weighting factor to internal electromagnetic modes. This weighting, dependent on the mode frequency measured in the interaction's rest frame, successfully makes several key one-loop calculations finite while maintaining Ward identity consistency. It suggests that localization effects can be modeled through such scale-dependent modifications of vacuum contributions.
main_problem: The work investigates whether localized electromagnetic interactions can be modeled by introducing an effective, object-relative ultraviolet weighting of internal quantum electrodynamics (QED) modes.
main_result: Applying this specific weighting successfully renders selected one-loop QED contributions UV finite while preserving a restricted form of the Ward identity. The results suggest that different physical observables may probe distinct effective localization scales.
method: The authors propose an ansatz for the weighting factor, $W(k; k_c)$, which depends on the object-relative covariant mode variable $u \cdot k$, and test its consistency by calculating one-loop corrections to key QED processes.
model_or_system: The theoretical framework is Quantum Electrodynamics (QED), focusing on how internal electromagnetic modes behave when interactions are assumed to be highly localized relative to a characteristic scale, $l_c$.
key_observables: Anomalous magnetic moment, Bethe-type low-energy Lamb shift estimate, and the Casimir effect.
important_parameters: Characteristic localization scale ($l_c$) leading to wave number $k_c$, and the object-relative mode frequency measured in the interaction's rest frame ($u \cdot k$).
main_assumptions: The weighting is introduced as a heuristic ansatz, not derived from an underlying action. The consistency check is restricted to one-loop diagrams where the weighting acts as a common scalar factor.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of modeling localized interactions via mode weighting, develops the object-relative covariant weighting ansatz based on heuristic arguments, proves its consistency with Ward identities at one loop, and validates it through four specific physical test cases.
why_interesting: Although focused on QED renormalization, the concept of introducing an 'effective' scale dependence into field theory calculations to tame UV divergences echoes themes in effective field theories relevant to AMO physics when considering short-range interactions or high-energy cutoffs.
